name: LIFELONG-SOTOPIA
description: Humans engage in lifelong social interactions through interacting with different people under different scenarios for different social goals. This requires social intelligence to gather information through a long time span and use it to navigate various social contexts effectively. Whether AI systems are also capable of this is understudied in the existing research. In this paper, we present a novel benchmark, LIFELONG-SOTOPIA, to perform a comprehensive evaluation of language agents by simulating multi-episode interactions. In each episode, the language agents role-play characters to achieve their respective social goals in randomly sampled social tasks. With LIFELONG-SOTOPIA, we find that goal achievement and believability of all of the language models that we test decline through the whole interaction. reputation: A very recent benchmark for long-horizon social-agent evaluation, it is not yet widely adopted but is notable for extending social simulation to lifelong multi-episode settings.
notes: New benchmark with limited community adoption so far; multi-episode social interaction makes it harder than standard single-turn dialogue benchmarks, and results depend on memory strategy and human/LLM judging setup.
